newsitem.title: USA: Sky Mall encouraging in-flight calls.
newsitem.headline: Sky Mall encouraging in-flight calls.

text.p: SkyMall Inc, the in-flight catalog company, sees substantial opportunities to grow revenue by encouraging passengers to order the merchandise while in flight, Chief Executive Officer Robert Worsley said on Wednesday.

Although the company has shown strong revenue growth for several years, Worsley said its average revenues of 9.3 cents per passenger remain well under the the $5 per passenger sales rate of the successful Duty Free in-flight sales industry.

For that reason, Worsley said at the Cruttenden Roth Growth Stock Conference here, SkyMall would seek to boost revenue growth by imitating the Duty Free marketing strategy, which includes offering discounts on merchandise and using flight attendants to promote the catalogs.

He said surveys show most of the company's customers believe in error that its catalog merchandise is priced higher than in home catalogues, and that only five percent of its customers place orders from the plane.
"We need to get the message out that the call (to order merchandise from the plane) is free," Worsley said.
Because the growth strategy is linked closely to boosting consumer awareness, he said, "we believe we can grow the business without significant capital requirements in the future."
